summary: The stop at zero-based step 30 is caused by the missing TIN_OPENER arm in the partially ported apply.c:doapply. C selects the opener and reaches the existing eat.c:use_tin_opener -> start_tin path; this is missing source behavior, not a tin-opening divergence.

source.branch: With usable hands and capacity, after getobj selects a valid object that survives retouch_object and is not a wand, spellbook, or coin, TIN_OPENER must set doapply’s result from use_tin_opener and then reach the common artifact-speech tail.
callers: Direct command: C cmd.c extcmdlist's 'a' entry (1677-1678) dispatches to doapply; JS extcmdlist_data.js's apply row is dispatched by cmd.js dispatchHandler -> runApplyCommand -> apply.js doapply (cmd.js 3302-3304, 5150-5151).

Queued C callers: cmd.c MCMD_LOCK_DOOR and MCMD_APPLY_SADDLE (4705, 4751); apply.c use_whip, use_pole, and use_grapple (2966, 3442, 3745); dig.c use_pick_axe (1104); iactions.c itemactions_pushkeys (156). These queue the same doapply command handled by the JS command dispatcher.
dependencies: eat.c use_tin_opener is already implemented in js/eat.js:1416-1442 and its ECMD result is consumed by doapply. It selects the tin and calls start_tin, whose existing JS implementation is js/eat.js:1260-1367.

The whole doapply function also has a missing LUMP_OF_ROYAL_JELLY arm: C calls apply.c use_royal_jelly and consumes its ECMD result (apply.c:4262-4264; definition 3616 onward), while JS doapply falls through to UnsupportedApplyError and js/apply.js dorub still refuses the same helper path (2218-2221). This is a separate arm from the selected case but must be resolved if completing every doapply branch under the callee-return rule.

The FLINT, LUCKSTONE, LOADSTONE, and TOUCHSTONE arm is also absent from the JS switch, although js/apply.js already implements use_stone (2041 onward); the doapply fallback currently refuses those named types. TOWEL is present as an explicit arm before the fallback, so its stale membership in DOAPPLY_UNPORTED_NAMED_ARMS does not block it.

The selected recording ends on start_tin setting the tin-opening occupation. It does not continue through a later opentin turn or tin consumption; the existing eat.c consume_tin path retains note_unported('eat.c cprefx') in js/eat.js and is beyond these three missing boundaries.

evidence: C source apply.c:4214-4424 defines the whole doapply function. Its explicit TIN_OPENER arm at 4364-4366 assigns res = use_tin_opener(obj), then the function reaches its shared artifact tail at 4419-4424. This is the complete source unit selected for a file-port.

The omission is visible in js/apply.js:4722-4958: no TIN_OPENER case exists; TIN_OPENER is object type 239 (js/objects.js:314), is listed in DOAPPLY_UNPORTED_NAMED_ARMS (js/apply.js:3867-3875), and throws UnsupportedApplyError in the default branch (4947-4950).

The saved evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261001125731-v16.json and manifest case wizard-applies-tin-opener-to-spinach-tin agree on first mismatch segment 0, step 30: JS stops before C handles the opener. C records 33 screens, 3440 RNG calls; the evaluation matches 30 screens/cursors and 3432 RNG calls, leaving exactly 3 unmatched screens.

The assigned C recording challenges/cases/v16/wizard-applies-tin-opener-to-spinach-tin.session.json shows the remaining boundaries: key o (step 30) yields “You now wield a tin opener.”; space (step 31) prompts “What do you want to open?”; p (step 32) yields “Using your tin opener you try to open the tin.” The first RNG call at step 32 is rn2(2)=1 in eat.c:start_tin (1750), so this input schedules the existing opening occupation instead of consuming the tin immediately.

C continuation is apply.c:4364-4366 -> eat.c:use_tin_opener (3097-3127) -> eat.c:start_tin (1723-1797). JS already wires the latter two at js/eat.js:1416-1442 and 1260-1367. The direct command caller is cmd.c:1677-1678 and js/cmd.js:3302-3304, 5150-5151; queued C entry sites are listed in source.callers.

nethack-c/patches/README.md describes recorder patches as deterministic runtime, sorting, RNG logging, and screen capture; rg found no doapply or use_tin_opener references in nethack-c/patches. The behavior owner is the upstream apply.c function.
